# Sakk

> Sakk stops an AI coding agent before it overspends, leaks a secret or force-pushes. It is a fail-closed pre-tool-use guard for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex, a daily spend cap for Claude Code (an estimate from local logs, not the invoice), a kill switch, a secret scanner for git, and a spend ledger for your own agent code. Local, zero dependencies, Node 20+ on macOS or Linux, Apache-2.0.

Install and check it in a project: `npm install -g @sakk-dev/sakk`, then `sakk guard install claude-code` (or `cursor`, `codex`), then `sakk doctor`. Set a daily cap with `sakk cap set 5 --zone Asia/Dubai`; see today's spend with `sakk spend`. Stop every guarded agent with `sakk halt --by <name>` and lift it with `sakk resume --by <name>`.

For your own AI app in any language, Sakk's spend gate runs inside the LiteLLM proxy (OpenAI compatible): `sakk init --cap 5`, then `sakk gateway init` (it needs LiteLLM 1.106.2 installed and prints the hash-locked install steps if not), start the written `~/.sakk/gateway/start.sh` with `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` and the provider key in its environment, and change one line in the app: `OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1`. If the gateway cannot get an answer from the ledger, it lets the call through by default with a warning, an `x-sakk-status: unmetered` header, a banner in `sakk ui` and a line in `sakk status`; those calls are not recorded or capped. `SAKK_ON_UNAVAILABLE=deny` refuses them instead. Over budget (402), unpriced models (403) and malformed requests (400) are always refused. The coding-agent guard and the library ledger stay fail-closed. Details: [integrations/litellm/README.md](integrations/litellm/README.md).

Sakk is a report-and-stop tool, not an agent platform: ccusage and Claude Code's `/cost` report spend; Sakk refuses the next call. Names given with `--by` are self-declared, and the cap stops the next call, not the one that crosses it.
